source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Assuming the client needs fairly little ongoing psychosocial support once they become medically stable on their current heart failure treatment regimen","B":"Focusing mainly on medication adherence alone during clinic visits, with comparatively little attention paid to the client's broader emotional needs","C":"A single conversation held once at the time of diagnosis, with fairly little planned follow-up offered to the client in the months that follow","D":"Providing ongoing emotional support, connecting the client with resources, and addressing the unique challenges of managing a chronic, potentially progressive cardiac condition"}}
source_row.rationale: Supporting a client's psychological adjustment to chronic heart failure includes providing ongoing emotional support, connecting them with relevant resources (such as support groups), and addressing the unique challenges of managing a chronic, potentially progressive condition, recognizing that this adjustment process continues throughout the disease course.
source_row.source_detail: Comprehensive Support for Chronic HF Adjustment
source_row.source_name: AHA — Psychosocial Support in Chronic Heart Failure
